p: the sidra of Vezos HaBerachah on Simchas Torah,
on one of the six weekdays
which were fixed specifically on Shabbos.
because the entire matter of the Written Torah
is only from the holiness from Above,
Therefore the reading of all the sidros of the Torah
"to know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you."
Except for the sidra "And this is the blessing
שֶׁהוּא עַל הֲכָנַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
which concerns the preparation of the Oral Torah,
that it be renewed in the hearts of the souls of Yisrael,
for each individual soul according to its level.
Therefore the main reading of this sidra
is specifically on the day of Simchas Torah,
for the renewal of words of Torah
which are prepared for the arousal of man's own action,
from the side of the awakening from below,
which is the aspect of the Oral Torah.
And one can say that this is also alluded to
in the particulars of the blessings
that he gave each tribe individually:
that words of Torah be renewed in their hearts,
for each one according to his root in the Torah.
And this is what it says (Devarim 33:6),
that he receive the vitality of his flow
in the letters of the Torah,
as is known, that every Jewish soul has
And likewise, "And this for Yehudah," etc. (ibid. 7),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ חֲזַ״ל (בָּבָא קַמָּא צב, א)
that he should deliberate in halachah
and bring the teachings to a conclusion in accordance with the halachah.
וַיֹּאמַר ה׳ מִסִּינַי בָּא וְגוֹמֵר (שָׁם, ב):
"And he said: Hashem came from Sinai," etc. (ibid. 2):
a preparation for acquiring the Torah in the heart.
which is the aspect of humility and lowliness,
as in the words of our Sages (Avos 1:1),
and as is known from the commentators
and as mentioned in Tanchuma, Parshas Noach (siman 3),
that the essential acquisition of the Oral Torah
from the pleasures of this world.
"And He shone forth from Seir to them":
וּכְדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קצג, א)
as brought in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 193a),
from the princes of the nations of the world,
And the matter of the gifts and presents
הַיְינוּ, כִּי בְּחִינַת כּוֹחוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו
is this: the aspect of Esav's power
was given to Yisrael according to the Torah;
that is, in this world it is necessary
that the aspect of anger exist,
which is the very essence of the kelipah of Esav;
"From the forest itself let the axe go into it."
וְלָזֶה נֶאֱמַר בִּשְׁמוּאֵל (שְׁמוּאֵל א טו, לג)
And regarding this it says of Shmuel (Shmuel I 15:33),
specifically the kind fitting for him.
Therefore it is stated with the expression "shone forth,"
which is only a slight shining
for the purpose of wiping out Amalek.
when the memory of Amalek will be erased entirely,
then the aspect of anger, too, will be abolished
this is the aspect of the power of Yishmael
which was also given to Yisrael,
and even more so, as the expression "appeared" implies;
will not be abolished even in the time to come;
for the delight of Torah learning.
וְזֶה רָמְזוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זַ״ל (קִידּוּשִׁין ל, ב):
And this our Sages alluded to (Kiddushin 30b):
that is, the yetzer hara of desire,
that is, that the taste of craving
which there is in this matter —
that this taste was given to transgressors,
he should bring into words of Torah.
"And He came from the holy myriads":
the reason the word "ve'asa" is stated
one can say that the "holy myriads"
who argued that it is not fitting
to give the inner dimension of the Torah to this world;
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הֵשִׁיב לָהֶם
and Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, answered them,
"Is there a yetzer hara among you?" —
meaning that the plain level of the Torah
that the inner dimension of the Torah too
and as our Sages said (Devarim Rabbah 8:6)
that nothing of it remained in heaven.
And this is the meaning of "ve'asa":
that, as it were, Hashem Himself
clothed Himself in the Torah among us;
and therefore this word is stated
which the ministering angels do not recognize,
so that they not be jealous of us.
